points.t: Recurrent lip, tongue or face swelling without hives in someone on ramipril, lisinopril or another ACE inhibitor.
ACE inhibitors block bradykinin breakdown; bradykinin leaks fluid into deep tissue, so histamine-based treatments work poorly.
Airway first (999 if needed); stop the ACE inhibitor permanently and record it; choose a non-ACE alternative with care.
Airway compromise; hereditary angioedema; ARB or sacubitril/valsartan cross-reactivity; DPP-4 inhibitors raising the risk.

points: **Triggers:** minor trauma/surgery, dental work and intubation can precipitate attacks. That fits this case (swelling a week after skin-tag removal), though the procedure is a trigger, not the cause.
Clinical: angioedema with **no urticaria**, on an ACE-i, not responding to antihistamine/steroid.

items.t: Tongue or throat swelling, voice change, stridor or difficulty swallowing: **999** now.
Stop the ACE inhibitor **permanently** even if the swelling has settled, and document it as an adverse reaction.

pearls.t: "Angioedema **without wheals** on an ACE-i = bradykinin. Antihistamines won't fix it — **stopping the ACE-i** will (eventually)."
Check every ACE-i patient on the medication review for previous facial or tongue swelling — patients often don't link it to a long-standing tablet.
The risk persists for years on treatment, so this is not just a "first-month" issue.
